source.title: Communication-Efficient Language Model Training Scales Reliably and Robustly: Scaling Laws for DiLoCo
source.authors: Zachary Charles; Gabriel Teston; Lucio M. Dery; Keith Rush; Nova Fallen; Zachary Garrett; A. Szlam; Arthur Douillard

record.tranche_reason: The study measures held-out language-model evaluation loss across model sizes, fits scaling laws, and tests extrapolation to larger runs; it also evaluates a different training regime, DiLoCo.
record.gate_note: The paper reports many hyperparameter sweeps and downstream benchmark results. Rows below focus on held-out loss scaling, extrapolation, overtraining, fit-form comparisons, and the downstream result relevant to V6. Other batch-size and downstream task sweeps are not included.
record.test_reason: The study fits L(N)≈AN^α to C4 held-out pretraining loss over 35M–2.4B parameters at D=20N, the method of the original sources. It then checks extrapolation by training 4B and 10B models. It also compares loss-fit functional forms on held-out 2.4B data. DiLoCo is a new training setting for the same measure.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that DiLoCo, like Data-Parallel, scales predictably with model size, with loss and hyperparameter laws that extrapolate to 4B/10B. They find DiLoCo M=1 beats Data-Parallel at all scales and DiLoCo M=2 beats it at 4B/10B. They find benefits robust to overtraining and synchronization cadence, and that more nuanced parametric forms predict held-out loss better than a pure joint power law. They recommend joint fits for hyperparameters.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses held-out pretraining evaluation loss and power-law fitting similar to the original scaling-law work, but applies it to DiLoCo as well as Data-Parallel, fixes tokens at D=20N for the main sweeps, and varies replica count and training hyperparameters.
record.method_sensitivity: Loss and hyperparameter outcomes vary with DiLoCo replica count M; the paper also reports that candidate loss-fit function forms yield different held-out residuals. Overtraining multiplier is varied in the Dolma experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: DiLoCo's loss relative to Data-Parallel improves monotonically with N. M=1 beats Data-Parallel at every size, and M=2 beats it at 2.4B, 4B and 10B.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Communication-efficient training methods (DiLoCo) follow loss scaling comparable to or steeper than data-parallel training.

fits_no_version.finding: DiLoCo M=1 has higher HellaSwag zero-shot accuracy than Data-Parallel, and the gap grows with batch size.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The optimizer variant (outer momentum) affects batch-size tolerance and downstream accuracy at fixed scale.

record.code_released: http://github.com/google-deepmind/nanodo (NanoDO is cited; study-specific code release not stated)
record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for the loss results. The main model-size sweep couples token budget to parameter count through D=20N, and the 4B and 10B results use predicted hyperparameters rather than extensive sweeps. Some relevant curves are only shown graphically.
record.rows_left_out: The paper also reports fitted hyperparameter laws (Tables 8–10), leave-one-out fit residuals (Table 11), additional 4B/10B training results under the fit methods already represented here (Table 5), overtraining results for DiLoCo M=2 and M=4, and further batch-size/downstream benchmark sweeps (Figures 4–5 and 14–19). These were not extracted as separate rows to keep the record within the 60-row limit and avoid duplicating the larger-run loss results.

untested.parts: Tokens are tied to parameters (D=20N), so N and D are not varied independently with the other non-bottlenecked. The fitted range is about 70× in N (35M–2.4B), under the several orders of magnitude V1 names.
Extrapolation reaches only about 4× beyond the largest fitted model (2.4B→10B), not orders of magnitude. Predicted loss values are not tabulated.
Not tested; the token budget is fixed at D=20N, taken from Chinchilla.
Not tested; shape co-varies with size and is never varied at fixed N.
Not tested; no other modality, repeated data, fine-tuning or transfer. Overtraining on text is treated under V1.
No downstream scaling law or accuracy-vs-loss fit. Zero-shot accuracies across scale are shown only in figures.
Parameter-counting conventions and comparison with published exponents are not tested. Compute-optimal split dependence is not tested.

missing.what: Zero-shot accuracy on HellaSwag, PIQA and Arc-Easy across 35M–2.4B, rising with scale (HellaSwag from about 0.27 to about 0.55). No fit is given; Arc-Easy is noted as noisy.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked r01–r28 to V1, but they are algorithm-comparison points; V1 rests on the r29–r33 fits. The overtraining rows were moved from V5 to V1. r58 does not test V6 predictability. In r54–r57, M is the DiLoCo replica count, so the form comparison mostly concerns how M enters. Only the +C term (r54 vs r55) speaks to bending from a pure power law. There is a minor text inconsistency: the text says DiLoCo M=4 is 0.26% worse at 2.4B, while Table 4 shows +0.3%. The paper does not report uncertainty.

versions.untested_parts: The main loss sweep uses the Chinchilla token budget D=20N, so parameters and tokens are not varied independently. It does not separately test loss scaling with tokens or compute while holding the other quantities non-bottlenecked.
Extrapolation is tested at 4B and 10B parameters for this model family and training setup; the paper does not test substantially larger scales or other model families.
The study fixes the token budget at D=20N and does not optimize parameter and token allocation under a fixed compute budget.
Architecture dimensions change with model size; the study does not compare depth, width, or other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
It tests overtraining on text, using Dolma and multipliers 1, 4, and 16. It does not test other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer.

Downstream results are reported for zero-shot benchmarks and some model scales and batch settings; the study does not establish a general downstream scaling law or model performance as a function of pretraining loss.

The study compares loss-fit functional forms and independent versus joint fits, but does not test effects of parameter-counting conventions, compare published exponents across studies, or test the compute-optimal parameter/token split.

tranche.reason: The study explicitly uses methodology similar to Kaplan and Hoffmann: model-size sweeps, held-out pretraining loss, power-law fitting, and extrapolation checks.

source_check.notes: Table 13 uses the held-out 2.4B data to select parameters among 256 initializations, so its residuals are validation results rather than an independent final test. The authors-conclusion paraphrase needs qualification: at 4B/10B, DiLoCo M=1 beats Data-Parallel only with joint-fit hyperparameters.
